draft.title: Judging research
card: research is valid when it measures what it claims to measure and its conclusion follows from the results.
a source is more trustworthy when it comes from people with relevant expertise, such as a peer-reviewed journal or a university team.
good researchers admit what they do not know. They report limits and avoid claiming their results prove something for certain.
good research considers possible errors and bias, such as a small or unusual sample or a funder who gains from a result.
draft.remember: Judge research by its validity, its source, its honesty about uncertainty and how it handles error and bias.

a.q: A study says it measures stress, but it only asks participants how many hours they slept. Which quality of good research is missing?
opts: Validity, as it does not measure what it claims to
Authority, as sleep studies need a famous author
Uncertainty, as it should have proved stress for certain
Bias, as all studies using sleep hours are biased
a.why: Sleep hours do not measure stress, so the study does not measure what it claims to. This is a problem of validity. Claiming certainty would make the research worse, not better.
a.clue: Does the measure match the thing being studied?

b.q: A drink company pays a team to test its energy drink on concentration. The report says the drink works, and does not mention its small sample of ten people. What is the best judgement?
opts: Be cautious, as bias and sample size were not considered
Trust it, as a company report has the most authority
Trust it, as a clear result means there is no uncertainty
Reject it, as any paid research is always false
b.why: The funder gains from the result and the small sample is not discussed, so possible bias and error were not considered. Paid research is not always false, but it needs careful checking.
b.clue: Ask who gains and whether limits were reported.

a.best: Validity, as it does not measure what it claims to

b.best: Be cautious, as bias and sample size were not considered
